Maccabi Fanatics | founded = {{Start date and age|df=yes|1906}}{{cite web |title=Maccabi in UEFA Website |url=https://www.uefa.com/nationalassociations/teams/57477--m-tel-aviv/ |access-date=30 August 2015 |website=UEFA}} | ground = [[Bloomfield Stadium]], [[Tel Aviv]], [[Israel]] | capacity = 29,400 | owner = [[Mitchell Goldhar]] | chairman = Jack Angelides | mgrtitle = Coach | manager = [[Kenny Miller]] | league = {{Israeli football updater|MTelAviv}} | season = {{Israeli football updater|MTelAviv2}} | position = {{Israeli football updater|MTelAviv3}} | current = 2025–26 Maccabi Tel Aviv F.C. season | website = {{URL|https://www.maccabi-tlv.co.il/en}} | pattern_la1 = _mta2526h | pattern_b1 = _mta2526h | pattern_ra1 = _mta2526h | pattern_sh1 = _mta2526h | pattern_so1 = _mta2526hl | leftarm1 = ffdf00 | body1 = ffdf00 | rightarm1 = ffdf00 | shorts1 = ffdf00 | socks1 = ffdf00 | pattern_ra2 = _mta2526a | pattern_b2 = _mta2526a | pattern_la2 = _mta2526a | pattern_sh2 = _mta2526a | pattern_so2 = | rightarm2 = 001450 | body2 = 001450 | leftarm2 = 001450 | shorts2 = 001450 | socks2 = 001450 | pattern_ra3 = _mta2526t | pattern_b3 = _mta2526t | pattern_la3 = _mta2526t | pattern_sh3 = _mta2526t | pattern_so3 = _mta2526tl | rightarm3 = | body3 = | leftarm3 = | shorts3 = | socks3 = }} {{Maccabi Tel Aviv sections}} '''Maccabi Tel Aviv Football Club''' ({{langx|he|מועדון כדורגל מכבי תל אביב}}; ''Moadon Kaduregel Maccabi Tel Aviv'') is an Israeli professional [[association football|football]] club from [[Tel Aviv]] and part of the [[Maccabi Tel Aviv|Maccabi Tel Aviv Sport Club]]. Founded in 1906 in [[Jaffa]] as the HaRishon Le Zion-Yafo Association, it is the oldest football club in Israel. With the establishment of the city of [[Tel Aviv]] in 1909, the club changed its name to Maccabi Tel Aviv. In 1922, it became the first [[Jews|Jewish]] football club to participate in local competitions. The [[wikt:Maccabee|meaning of the name Maccabi]] forms an integral part of the character of the team, which took the [[Star of David]] as their logo to represent the Jewish people. Maccabi Tel Aviv have won more titles than any other Israeli club, winning 26 [[Israeli Premier League|League Championships]], 24 [[Israel State Cup|State Cups]], 8 [[Toto Cup|Toto (League) Cups]],{{cite web |title=Maccabi Titels |url=http://www.maccabi-tlv.co.il/en/the-club/honours/ |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150817043736/http://www.maccabi-tlv.co.il/en/the-club/honours/ |archive-date=17 August 2015 |website=Maccabi Tel Aviv Official Website |publisher=Maccabi Tel Aviv}} and 2 [[AFC Champions League|Asian Champion Club Tournaments]] before Israel were expelled from the [[Asian Football Confederation|AFC]] in 1974. Maccabi Tel Aviv is the only football team that has never been relegated from the Israeli Premier League, the only Israeli club to have achieved a domestic treble, and one of only three Israeli teams ever to progress to the [[UEFA Champions League]] group stage. The club is named after the [[Maccabees]] and invests in the development and nurturing of young talent: the club runs three [[Youth system|football academies]] in the Tel Aviv area as part of its youth programme, working with over 750 children aged 6–15, as well as running 17 youth teams with 400 players between 9 and 19 years old. These teams tend to compete very successfully in local and national leagues.{{cite web |title=Youth Academy |url=http://www.maccabi-tlv.co.il/en/academy/youth-teams/ |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150817211138/http://www.maccabi-tlv.co.il/en/academy/youth-teams/ |archive-date=17 August 2015 |access-date=30 August 2015 |website=Maccabi Tel Aviv Official Website |publisher=Maccabi Tel Aviv}}"}}
